pass_a_gloss: …my son, you went up.' And the nations were bound in him unloosably. Therefore let us also be bound to Christ unloosably. If at all we strive to be saved and to be profited from his feasts, he himself also will raise us together with Lazarus from our dead works, those that came about without him. So let us dine with him in Bethany, which is interpreted 'house of the obedience'; so fittingly let us gather our thoughts from the captivity of the forgetting, with the sense-organs of the body, shouting and saying: 'Hosanna in the highest; blessed the one coming in the name of the Lord', to enter into his own Jerusalem, not on account of suffering as then, but that he may save her and be glorified by her, as David calls out to her, saying: 'Commend, Jerusalem, the Lord; praise your God, Zion.' A second time he said 'commend' and 'praise', with soul and body, 'because he strengthened the bars of your gates', which are faith, hope, love…
pass_b_english: …my son, you went up” (Genesis 49:9). And the nations were bound fast in Him, never to be loosed. So let us too be bound to Christ, never to be loosed. If we strive at all to be saved and to profit from His feasts, He in turn will raise us together with Lazarus from our dead works (Hebrews 9:14), the works done without Him.

So let us dine with Him in Bethany (John 12:2), which means “house of obedience”; so let us fittingly gather our thoughts, together with the senses of the body, out of the captivity of forgetfulness, crying out and saying: “Hosanna in the highest; blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord” (Matthew 21:9), who comes to enter His own Jerusalem, not to suffer as He did then, but to save her and to be glorified by her, as David calls out to her, saying: “Extol the Lord, O Jerusalem; praise your God, O Zion” (Psalm 147:12).
He said it twice, “extol” and “praise,” with soul and body, “for He has strengthened the bars of your gates” (Psalm 147:13), which are faith, hope, love…
